rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Go-Stop (Hanafuda) - Quick Rules 1.1 Overview 1.2 Gameplay 1.3 Card Types & Scoring 1.4 Go or Stop? 1.5 Strategic Special Rules Go-Stop (Hanafuda) - Quick Rules Overview Players: Ideally 3 players (2-player variants exist). Deck: Hanafuda deck (48 cards, 12 suits/months). Objective: Be the first to reach a minimum point threshold (usually 3 points) and decide whether to continue ("Go") or end the round ("Stop"). Gameplay On your turn, perform the following steps: Play from Hand: Match a card from your hand with a card of the same suit (month) on the table. If no match exists, discard it face up. Draw from Deck: Flip the top card of the draw pile. If it matches a card on the table, you take both. Collect: Any matches made are placed face up in your scoring area, categorized by type. Card Types & Scoring Brights (Gwang - 5 cards): 3 cards = 3 pts (if "Rain-Bright" is included: 2 pts), 4 cards = 4 pts, all 5 cards = 15 pts. Animals (Yul - 9 cards): 5 cards = 1 pt, each additional = +1 pt. Special (Godori): The 3 specific bird cards (Jan, Feb, Aug) together = 5 pts . Ribbons (Ti - 10 cards): 5 ribbons = 1 pt, each additional = +1 pt. Red Ribbons (Hong-dan): 3 red ribbons with writing (Jan, Feb, Mar) = 3 pts . Blue Ribbons (Cheong-dan): 3 blue ribbons (Jun, Sep, Oct) = 3 pts . Grass Ribbons (Cho-dan): 3 red ribbons without writing (Apr, May, Jul) = 3 pts . Chaff (Pi - 24+ cards): 10 cards = 1 pt, each additional = +1 pt. (Double-Pi count as 2 cards). Go or Stop? When you reach at least 3 points (7 points in 2-player games), you must announce: Stop: The round ends immediately, and you win your score. Go: Play continues. You gain bonuses (+1 pt for "1-Go" and "2-Go", score doubling starting at "3-Go"). If you call "Go" and an opponent scores before you "Stop," you lose everything ("Go-bak"). Strategic Special Rules Puck (Bomb): If you hold 3 cards of a suit in hand and the 4th is on the table, you can "bomb" the suit and take all four. You draw two cards from the deck afterwards. Kiss (Chok): If the card you play from hand and the card you draw from the deck both match the same card on the table, you take all three.

[Rating: 4/10] A more elaborate version of Koi-Koi, losing a fair deal of its elegance with the addition of point thresholds, stacks, bombs, jokers, multipliers and captures. Other differences include lack of monthly cards, potentially playing all cards in the deck in a single hand, extra bird and ribbon combinations but not boar-deer-butterfly, variable point kasu, three-player games with potentially convoluted asymmetric payouts, and a hundred local house rules (which is probably also the case for Koi-Koi).

[Rating: 4/10] It's all luck. Fine for a gambling game, which is what it is intended to be, but there are other traditional gambling games I'd rather play.

[Rating: 5/10] Great fun, and really easy when you get the hang of scoring.  Very frustrating not having your cards come up.  Lots of fun foiling players who push their luck with "Go!" calls.   Multiple paths to victory, screwage, and some gambling:  we have a winner!
